I've got my bed, a desk crammed with books, and a few plants dotted around. I suppose what I love most is how peaceful it is when I want to switch off.
questions.uzSampleA1: Mening xonam kichkina. Menda bitta karovat bor. Menda bitta stol bor. Bu mening xonam.

questions.uzSampleB1: Mening xonam juda kichkina, lekin u qulay. Albatta, karovatim bor va uy vazifalarini bajaradigan stolim ham bor. Yana ko'p kitoblari bor kitob javonim ham bor. Menga xonam yoqadi, chunki u yerda tinch, shuning uchun u yerda dam olishim mumkin. O'ylaymanki, bu men uchun yaxshi joy.

Menda karavot, stol va ancha yaxshi kitob javoni bor. Men, shuningdek, uni ba'zi plakatlar va o'simliklar bilan shaxsiylashtirishga harakat qildim. Garchi u eng katta xona bo'lmasa-da, u o'z maqsadiga yaxshi xizmat qiladi va men odatda u yerda vaqt o'tkazishdan zavqlanaman.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Tell me about your room.
idioms: a tidy room reflects a tidy mind - "tartibli xona tartibli ongni aks ettiradi"
"Home is where the heart is" - "Uy yurak bo'lgan joyda"
sentenceStarters: "My room is my personal space where I..." - "Mening xonam mening shaxsiy joyim, u yerda men..."
"Honestly speaking, I've decorated it to reflect..." - "Rostini aytsam, men uni ... aks ettirish uchun bezadim..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
My room is my personal sanctuary where I spend most of my time when I'm at home. It's not particularly large, but it's incredibly cozy and perfectly suited to my needs.
The walls are painted in a calming shade of light blue, which helps me relax after a long day. I have a comfortable bed in one corner, a wooden desk where I study, and a bookshelf filled with my favorite novels and textbooks.
What I love most about my room is the natural lighting. There's a large window that lets in plenty of sunlight during the day. I've also added some plants to liven up the space. As they say, "A tidy room reflects a tidy mind," so I always try to keep it organized.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening xonam – bu mening shaxsiy panohim, uyda bo'lganimda vaqtimning ko'p qismini shu yerda o'tkazaman. U unchalik katta emas, lekin juda shinam va mening ehtiyojlarimga juda mos.

Devorlar och ko'k rangning tinchlantiruvchi soyasida bo'yalgan, bu menga uzoq kundan keyin dam olishga yordam beradi. Bir burchakda qulay karovatim, o'qiydigan yog'och stolim va sevimli romanlarim va darsliklarim bilan to'ldirilgan kitob javonim bor.

Menga xonamning eng yoqadigan jihati – tabiiy yorug'lik. Katta deraza bor, u kunduzi ko'p quyosh nurini kiritadi. Men, shuningdek, makonni jonlantirish uchun bir nechta o'simliklar qo'shdim. Aytishlaricha, "Ozoda xona - ozoda ongning aksidir", shuning uchun men uni doimo tartibli saqlashga harakat qilaman.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - What time do you usually get up?
idioms: the early bird catches the worm - "erta turgan qushni ishi o'ngidan keladi"
sentenceStarters: "I typically wake up around..." - "Men odatda ... atrofida uyg'onaman..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I typically wake up around 6:30 in the morning on weekdays. I'm definitely more of a morning person, and I find that starting my day early helps me be more productive.
My morning routine is fairly consistent. After my alarm goes off, I usually spend a few minutes stretching before getting out of bed. Then I head to the kitchen to make myself a cup of coffee, which really helps me wake up properly.
On weekends, however, I tend to sleep in a bit – maybe until 8 or 9 o'clock. It's nice to have that extra rest. As the saying goes, "The early bird catches the worm," but occasionally we all need a lie-in!
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men odatda ish kunlari ertalab soat 6:30 atrofida uyg'onaman. Men aniqrog'i ertalabki odamman va ertalab kunimni boshlash menga unumliroq bo'lishga yordam beradi.

Mening ertalabki odatim ancha bir xil. Budilnik jiringlagandan so'ng, men odatda o'rnimdan turishdan oldin bir necha daqiqa cho'zilaman. Keyin men o'zimga bir chashka qahva tayyorlash uchun oshxonaga boraman, bu menga yaxshilab uyg'onishga yordam beradi.

Dam olish kunlari esa, men biroz uzoqroq uxlashga harakat qilaman – balki soat 8 yoki 9 gacha. Qo'shimcha dam olish juda yaxshi. Maqol aytganidek, "Ertalab turgan qush tumshug'ini to'ydirar", lekin ba'zida hammamizga biroz uxlab olish kerak!

questions.prompt: What do you do to stay healthy?
questions.sampleA2: I eat healthy food and I do exercise. I like to eat fruit and vegetables. I also walk my dog because it is good for me.
questions.sampleB1: I try to stay healthy by doing some exercise. For example, I go to the gym twice a week. I also try to eat healthy food, like vegetables and fruit. I think it's important to drink enough water too.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I try to look after myself without going overboard. I go for a run a few times a week, and I make a point of eating a balanced diet with plenty of fruit and veg. The thing is, I've got a bit of a sweet tooth, so cutting down on sugar is my biggest challenge. Getting enough sleep helps too.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men sog'lom ovqatlar yeyman va mashq qilaman. Mevalar va sabzavotlar yeyishni yaxshi ko'raman. Yana itimni sayr qildirishga olib chiqaman, chunki bu men uchun foydali.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men mashqlar bajarish orqali sog'lom bo'lishga harakat qilaman.
Masalan, haftada ikki marta sport zaliga boraman.
Shuningdek, sabzavot va mevalar kabi sog'lom ovqatlarni iste'mol qilishga harakat qilaman.
Menimcha, yetarli miqdorda suv ichish ham muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Xo'sh, men bir necha xil usullar orqali sog'lig'imga ongli ravishda g'amxo'rlik qilishga harakat qilaman. Birinchidan, men muntazam jismoniy faollikni o'z kun tartibimga kiritishga harakat qilaman. Men sport zalining katta muxlisi emasman, shuning uchun piyoda sayr qilish yoki velosipedda yurish kabi narsalarni afzal ko'raman. Shuningdek, men ovqatlanishimga e'tibor beraman, butun oziq-ovqatlarga e'tibor qarataman va qayta ishlangan gazaklar iste'molini cheklayman. Bu har doim ham oson emas, lekin men bu kichik o'zgarishlar umumiy farovonligimga katta ta'sir ko'rsatishini aniqladim.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - What do you do to stay healthy?
idioms: "An apple a day keeps the doctor away" - "Kuniga bitta olma shifokorni uzoqlashtiradi"
sentenceStarters: "I try to maintain a healthy lifestyle by..." - "Men sog'lom turmush tarzini ... orqali saqlashga harakat qilaman..."
"From my perspective, staying healthy requires..." - "Mening nuqtai nazarimdan, sog'lom qolish ... talab qiladi..."
"I firmly believe that physical activity is essential..." - "Men qat'iy ishonamanki, jismoniy faoliyat zarur..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I try to maintain a healthy lifestyle through a combination of regular exercise, balanced nutrition, and adequate rest.
Firstly, I make sure to exercise at least three times a week. I usually go jogging in the mornings and do some strength training at home. Physical activity definitely helps me feel more energetic and reduces stress.
Additionally, I pay close attention to what I eat. I try to include plenty of fruits, vegetables, and lean proteins in my diet while limiting processed foods and sugary drinks. I also drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Finally, I prioritize getting enough sleep – usually around seven to eight hours per night. As they say, "Health is wealth," and I firmly believe that taking care of your body is one of the best investments you can make.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men muntazam mashq qilish, muvozanatli ovqatlanish va yetarli dam olish orqali sog'lom turmush tarzini saqlashga harakat qilaman.

Birinchidan, haftada kamida uch marta mashq qilishga harakat qilaman. Odatda ertalab yuguraman va uyda kuch mashqlarini bajaraman. Jismoniy faollik menga ko'proq kuch beradi va stressni kamaytiradi.

Bundan tashqari, men nima yeyayotganimga katta e'tibor beraman. Ratsionimga ko'p miqdorda meva, sabzavot va kam yog'li oqsillarni kiritishga, qayta ishlangan mahsulotlar va shirin ichimliklarni cheklashga harakat qilaman. Shuningdek, kun davomida ko'p suv ichib, organizmni suv bilan ta'minlab turaman.

Nihoyat, men yetarlicha uxlashga, odatda kechasi yetti-sakkiz soat uxлашга ustunlik beraman. Aytishlaricha, "Sog'lik - boylik", va men o'z tanangizga g'amxo'rlik qilish eng yaxshi sarmoyalardan biri ekanligiga qat'iy ishonaman.

questions.sampleB2: Both pictures depict scenes of food shopping, though in markedly different environments. In the first image, a young family is browsing in a bright, modern supermarket. The dad is carrying his daughter on his back, who's reaching for items on the dairy shelves, while the mum pushes a shopping trolley full of groceries. The second photo, in contrast, shows a woman at a bustling open-air market on a sunny day. She’s paying by card for some fresh tomatoes. There are crates of colourful produce in front of her, with a sign indicating everything is 'one hundred percent organic'. This highlights the two distinct ways people shop for food today.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: "Get more bang for your buck" - "Pulingiz uchun ko'proq qiymat olish"

questions.sampleAnswer:
In these two pictures, I can see different shopping environments that represent two distinctly different ways of buying groceries.
In the first image, there's a couple shopping in what appears to be a modern supermarket. They're standing in an aisle with neatly organized shelves full of products. The man is wearing a plaid shirt and the woman is in a pink top. They have a shopping cart and seem to be carefully selecting items from the refrigerated section. The atmosphere looks clean, well-lit, and very organized.
The second picture shows a completely different scene – an open-air market or farmer's market. A woman is purchasing fresh produce directly from a vendor. We can see colorful vegetables like tomatoes, eggplants, and various other items displayed in wooden crates. The interaction appears more personal, with the buyer and seller engaging directly.
These images effectively illustrate the contrast between modern retail and traditional markets. Each has its own charm and appeals to different consumer preferences.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki suratda men oziq-ovqat mahsulotlarini sotib olishning ikki xil usulini aks ettiruvchi turli xarid qilish muhitlarini ko'rishim mumkin.

Birinchi suratda zamonaviy supermarketga o'xshagan joyda xarid qilayotgan er-xotinni ko'rish mumkin. Ular mahsulotlarga to'la, tartibli javonlar bilan qator bo'ylab turishibdi. Erkak katakli ko'ylakda, ayol esa pushti rangli topda. Ularda xarid qilish aravachasi bor va ular muzlatilgan bo'limdan mahsulotlarni diqqat bilan tanlayotganga o'xshaydi. Atmosfera toza, yaxshi yoritilgan va juda tartibli ko'rinadi.

Ikkinchi suratda butunlay boshqacha manzara – ochiq osmon ostidagi bozor yoki fermerlar bozori tasvirlangan. Bir ayol sotuvchidan to'g'ridan-to'g'ri yangi mahsulotlar sotib olmoqda. Biz pomidor, baqlajon va boshqa turli xil narsalar yog'och qutilarda namoyish etilgan rang-barang sabzavotlarni ko'rishimiz mumkin. Muloqot yanada shaxsiy ko'rinadi, xaridor va sotuvchi bevosita muloqot qilishadi.

Bu suratlar zamonaviy chakana savdo va an'anaviy bozorlar o'rtasidagi farqni samarali tarzda ko'rsatib beradi. Ularning har biri o'ziga xos jozibaga ega va turli xaridorlarning didiga mos keladi.

questions.prompt: What are the advantages of shopping in supermarkets compared to open-air markets?
questions.sampleA1: Supermarket good. Market... maybe not good. Supermarket easy.
questions.sampleA2: Supermarkets are good. They have many things. And it is inside, not outside. But markets are fun, and maybe cheaper.
questions.sampleB1: I think supermarkets are better than markets in some ways. For example, they have everything in one place, so it's easier. Also, they are usually open longer. However, markets can be more interesting and have fresher food.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the main advantage has to be convenience. In a supermarket, you can pick up everything under one roof in a single trip. On top of that, they're open all hours, the prices are clearly marked, and you can pay by card. To be fair, you do miss out on the charm of a market, but for sheer efficiency, supermarkets win hands down.
questions.uzSampleA1: Supermarket yaxshi. Bozor... balki yaxshi emas. Supermarket oson.
questions.uzSampleA2: Supermarketlar yaxshi. Ularda ko'p narsalar bor. Va u ichkarida, tashqarida emas. Lekin bozorlar qiziqarli va balki arzonroqdir.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, supermarketlar ba'zi jihatlarda bozorlardan yaxshiroq.
Masalan, ularda hamma narsa bir joyda bo'ladi, shuning uchun osonroq.
Shuningdek, ular odatda uzoqroq vaqt ochiq bo'ladi.
Biroq, bozorlar qiziqarliroq bo'lishi va yangi mahsulotlarga ega bo'lishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2: Supermarketlarning afzalliklari, albatta, bor. Bitta aniq foyda - bu qulaylik. Siz mahsulotlarning kengroq tanlovini topishingiz mumkin, va ularning ochilish soatlari odatda ochiq osmon ostidagi bozorlarga qaraganda ancha uzunroq va ishonchliroq bo'ladi. Supermarketlar narx va sifat nazorati nuqtai nazaridan ham ko'proq bashorat qilinadigan xarid tajribasini taklif etadi. Biroq, siz bozorda topishingiz mumkin bo'lgan o'ziga xos mahalliy mahsulotlarni topish imkoniyatini va jozibasini yo'qotasiz.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the advantages of shopping in supermarkets compared to open-air markets?
sentenceStarters: "One of the main advantages is..." - "Asosiy afzalliklardan biri..."
"From a practical standpoint, supermarkets offer..." - "Amaliy nuqtai nazardan, supermarketlar ... taklif qiladi..."
"I believe that modern retail provides..." - "Menimcha, zamonaviy savdo ... beradi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Shopping in supermarkets offers several distinct advantages compared to open-air markets.
Firstly, convenience is a major benefit. Supermarkets are typically open for longer hours, sometimes even 24/7, allowing customers to shop whenever it suits them. Everything is under one roof, so you can buy groceries, household items, and personal care products all in one trip.
Secondly, supermarkets offer a wider variety of products. You can find both local and imported goods, seasonal items, and specialty products that might not be available at traditional markets. The products are also clearly labeled with prices and expiration dates.
Additionally, supermarkets provide a more comfortable shopping experience. They're air-conditioned, well-organized, and offer shopping carts and baskets. You don't have to worry about weather conditions like rain or extreme heat.
Finally, supermarkets often accept various payment methods including credit cards and digital payments, whereas many open-air markets only accept cash. They also frequently offer loyalty programs and discounts.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Supermarketlarda xarid qilish ochiq havoda joylashgan bozorlarga nisbatan bir qator aniq afzalliklarni taqdim etadi.

Birinchidan, qulaylik asosiy ustunlik hisoblanadi. Supermarketlar odatda uzoqroq vaqt davomida, ba'zan hatto 24/7 ishlaydi, bu esa xaridorlarga o'zlariga mos kelgan vaqtda xarid qilish imkoniyatini beradi. Hamma narsa bir tom ostida bo'ladi, shuning uchun siz bir safarda oziq-ovqat, uy-ro'zg'or buyumlari va shaxsiy parvarishlash mahsulotlarini sotib olishingiz mumkin.

Ikkinchidan, supermarketlar mahsulotlarning kengroq assortimentini taklif etadi. Siz ham mahalliy, ham import qilingan mahsulotlarni, mavsumiy mahsulotlarni va an'anaviy bozorlarda mavjud bo'lmasligi mumkin bo'lgan maxsus mahsulotlarni topishingiz mumkin. Mahsulotlar narxlari va yaroqlilik muddati bilan aniq belgilangan.

Bundan tashqari, supermarketlar yanada qulay xarid qilish tajribasini ta'minlaydi. Ular konditsionerlangan, yaxshi tashkil etilgan va xarid qilish aravachalari va savatlarini taklif qiladi. Siz yomg'ir yoki haddan tashqari issiqlik kabi ob-havo sharoitlari haqida tashvishlanishingiz shart emas.

Nihoyat, supermarketlar ko'pincha kredit kartalari va raqamli to'lovlar, jumladan, turli xil to'lov usullarini qabul qiladi, ko'plab ochiq havoda joylashgan bozorlar esa faqat naqd pulni qabul qiladi. Ular, shuningdek, tez-tez sodiqlik dasturlari va chegirmalarni taklif qilishadi.

questions.prompt: How can shopping habits reflect cultural differences?
questions.sampleA1: I like shop. I buy food. My friend buy clothes.
questions.sampleA2: I go to the shops. People buy different things. Some people buy food and some buy clothes. I think it's because they like different things.
questions.sampleB1: I think shopping habits are different in different countries. For example, in some places, people go to the market every day to buy fresh food. In other places, people go to the supermarket once a week. Also, what people buy depends on their culture and what they like to eat.
questions.sampleB2: Well, shopping habits can say a great deal about a culture. In some countries, people pop down to a local market every single day for fresh ingredients, and it's almost a social ritual. Elsewhere, folks would rather do one big weekly shop at a supermarket. On top of that, what ends up in the basket reflects local tastes, traditions and even religious beliefs.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men xarid qilishni yaxshi ko'raman. Men oziq-ovqat sotib olaman. Mening do'stim kiyim sotib oladi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men do'konlarga boraman. Odamlar har xil narsalar sotib olishadi. Ba'zi odamlar ovqat sotib olishadi, ba'zilari esa kiyim. Menimcha, buning sababi ularga har xil narsalar yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, xarid qilish odatlari turli mamlakatlarda har xil.
Masalan, ba'zi joylarda odamlar har kuni bozorda yangi oziq-ovqat sotib olishadi. Boshqa joylarda esa, odamlar haftada bir marta supermarketga borishadi. Shuningdek, odamlarning nima sotib olishi ularning madaniyati va nima yeyishni yoqtirishiga bog'liq.
questions.uzSampleB2: Xarid qilish odatlari madaniy farqlarni aniq ko'rsatadi. Misol uchun, odamlarning oziq-ovqat xarid qilish usuli juda farq qilishi mumkin. Ba'zi madaniyatlarda har kuni yangi, mahalliy mahsulotlarni kichik do'konlar yoki bozorlardan sotib olishga katta e'tibor beriladi. Bu odamlar supermarketda haftalik katta xaridlarni afzal ko'radigan madaniyatlardan farq qiladi. Shuningdek, mashhur yoki oson topiladigan tovarlar turlari mahalliy did va an'analarni aks ettiradi. Siz ba'zi ziravorlar yoki ingredientlarning kengroq assortimentini ularni pishirishda keng qo'llaniladigan mamlakatlarda topishingiz mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - How can shopping habits reflect cultural differences?
idioms: when in Rome, do as the Romans do - "Rimda bo'lsang, rimliklar kabi qil"
sentenceStarters: "Shopping habits can reveal a lot about..." - "Xarid odatlari ... haqida ko'p narsani ochib beradi..."
"From a cultural perspective, we can observe..." - "Madaniy nuqtai nazardan, biz ... kuzatishimiz mumkin..."
"Different societies approach shopping in unique ways..." - "Turli jamiyatlar xaridga o'ziga xos usullar bilan yondashadi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Shopping habits can significantly reflect cultural differences in numerous ways.
Firstly, the preference between supermarkets and traditional markets often varies by culture. In many Asian and Middle Eastern countries, people still prefer visiting local bazaars where they can haggle over prices and build relationships with vendors. This reflects cultures that value personal interaction and community ties. In contrast, Western cultures often prioritize efficiency and convenience, hence the popularity of supermarkets.
Secondly, what people buy reveals cultural values. Some cultures emphasize buying fresh ingredients daily, as seen in Mediterranean and Asian cuisines, while others prefer bulk shopping for the week. The types of products available also differ – you'll find different spices, ingredients, and brands depending on the region.
Furthermore, shopping frequency varies culturally. In some European countries, people enjoy daily visits to local markets as a social activity, whereas in others, weekly shopping trips are more common.
Finally, payment preferences and bargaining practices differ. In many cultures, negotiating prices is expected and even enjoyed, while in others, fixed pricing is the norm.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Xarid qilish odatlari madaniy farqlarni ko'plab usullar bilan sezilarli darajada aks ettirishi mumkin.

Birinchidan, supermarketlar va an'anaviy bozorlar o'rtasidagi tanlov ko'pincha madaniyatga qarab farq qiladi. Ko'pgina Osiyo va Yaqin Sharq mamlakatlarida odamlar narxlarni kelishib olish va sotuvchilar bilan munosabatlar o'rnatish uchun mahalliy bozorlarga borishni afzal ko'rishadi. Bu shaxsiy muloqot va jamiyat aloqalarini qadrlaydigan madaniyatlarni aks ettiradi. Aksincha, G'arb madaniyati ko'pincha samaradorlik va qulaylikka ustunlik beradi, shuning uchun supermarketlar mashhur.

Ikkinchidan, odamlarning nima sotib olishi madaniy qadriyatlarni ochib beradi. Ba'zi madaniyatlar O'rta yer dengizi va Osiyo oshxonalarida ko'rinib turganidek, har kuni yangi mahsulotlar sotib olishga urg'u beradi, boshqalari esa bir hafta uchun ommaviy xarid qilishni afzal ko'radi. Mavjud mahsulot turlari ham farq qiladi - mintaqaga qarab turli xil ziravorlar, ingredientlar va brendlarni topasiz.

Bundan tashqari, xarid qilish chastotasi madaniy jihatdan farq qiladi. Ba'zi Yevropa mamlakatlarida odamlar mahalliy bozorlarga har kuni tashrif buyurishdan ijtimoiy faoliyat sifatida zavqlanishadi, boshqalarida esa haftalik xarid qilish odatiy hol.

Nihoyat, to'lov usullari va savdolashish amaliyotlari farq qiladi. Ko'pgina madaniyatlarda narxlarni kelishish kutiladi va hatto zavq bilan qabul qilinadi, boshqalarida esa qat'iy narxlar me'yor hisoblanadi.

questions.prompt: Tell me about the time when you shared a secret with another person.
questions.sampleA1: I have a secret. I tell my friend. She is happy.
questions.sampleA2: I have a secret. It was about my birthday party. I told my sister, and she was happy for me. But she didn't tell anyone else, because it was a secret!
questions.sampleB1: I remember once I told my friend a secret. It was about a boy I liked. I was very nervous to tell her, but I trusted her. She didn't tell anyone else, and she gave me good advice. I think it's important to keep secrets.
questions.sampleB2: Right, well, I'd like to tell you about a time I shared a secret with my closest friend, back when we were at university. She's always been the one person I can turn to, no matter what. The thing is, I'd secretly decided to drop out of my course and switch to something completely different, but I hadn't breathed a word of it to my family. It had been eating away at me for weeks, and I desperately needed to get it off my chest. So, one evening over coffee, I just came clean and told her everything. To be honest, I was terrified she'd judge me or, worse, let it slip to someone else. But she listened without interrupting, and that meant the world to me. As for how I felt afterwards, it was an enormous relief, like a huge weight had been lifted off my shoulders. Bottling something up like that is exhausting, so finally saying it out loud was incredibly freeing. On top of that, she gave me some really sound advice that helped me make up my mind. As for keeping other people's secrets, I honestly think it's absolutely crucial. When someone confides in you, they're putting their trust in you, and betraying that would be a real stab in the back. Trust takes years to build but seconds to destroy. I always make a point of being someone people can rely on, because at the end of the day, loyalty is what real friendship is built on.
questions.uzSampleA1: Mening sirim bor. Men do'stimga aytaman. U xursand.
questions.uzSampleA2: Mening bir sirim bor. Bu mening tug'ilgan kunim haqida edi. Men singlimga aytdim va u mendan xursand bo'ldi. Lekin u hech kimga aytmadi, chunki bu sir edi!
questions.uzSampleB1: Esimda, bir marta do'stimga bir sirni aytgan edim. Bu menga yoqqan bir bola haqida edi. Unga aytishdan juda hayajonlangan edim, lekin unga ishondim. U hech kimga aytmadi va menga yaxshi maslahat berdi. Menimcha, sirlarni saqlash muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Bir marta ishxonadagi hamkasbim bilan sirimni bo'lishgan edim. Men ishimni tashlab ketish haqida o'ylayotgan edim, lekin hali aniq emas edi. Men unga ishonishim mumkinligini his qildim, shuning uchun unga dardimni aytdim. Unga aytayotganda biroz asabiylashdim, lekin keyin yengil tortdim. U sirimni saqladi, bu meni juda xursand qildi. O'ylashimcha, sirlarni saqlash ishonchni mustahkamlash uchun muhim, va men doimo odamlar ishonishi mumkin bo'lgan inson bo'lishga harakat qilaman.

bulletPoints: Tell me about the time when you shared a secret with another person.
How did you feel after sharing it?
How important is it to keep other people's secrets?
questions.sampleAnswer:
I remember a time when I shared a personal secret with my best friend about my career plans. I was considering changing my field of study, but I hadn't told anyone in my family yet.
Before sharing, I felt incredibly anxious and burdened by keeping this decision to myself. After I finally opened up to my friend, I felt an immense relief – like a weight had been lifted off my shoulders. It was genuinely liberating to have someone to discuss my thoughts and concerns with.
My friend listened attentively, offered valuable advice, and most importantly, kept my secret safe until I was ready to tell others. This experience reinforced our mutual trust.
As for keeping other people's secrets, I believe it's absolutely essential. When someone trusts you with a secret, they're showing deep trust and vulnerability. Betraying that trust can permanently damage relationships. As the saying goes, "Trust takes years to build, seconds to break, and forever to repair." Being a trustworthy person is one of the most valuable qualities one can have.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Esimda, bir marta eng yaqin do'stim bilan o'z kareramga oid rejalarim haqida shaxsiy sirimni bo'lishgan edim. Men o'qish sohamni o'zgartirishni o'ylayotgan edim, lekin bu haqda oilamdagilarga hali aytmagan edim.

Bo'lishishdan oldin, bu qarorni o'zimda saqlaganim uchun o'zimni juda xavotirda va og'ir yuk ostida his qildim. Do'stimga nihoyat ochilganimdan so'ng, o'zimni juda yengil his qildim – go'yo yelkamdan tog' ag'darilgandek bo'ldi. O'z fikrlarim va tashvishlarimni muhokama qiladigan odamning borligi chinakam ozodlik edi.

Do'stim diqqat bilan tingladi, qimmatli maslahatlar berdi va eng muhimi, men boshqalarga aytishga tayyor bo'lgunimcha sirimni saqladi. Bu tajriba o'zaro ishonchimizni mustahkamladi.

Boshqalarning sirlarini saqlashga kelsak, menimcha, bu juda muhim. Kimdir sizga sirini ishonib topshirsa, ular chuqur ishonch va zaiflikni ko'rsatadilar. Bu ishonchni xiyonat qilish munosabatlarga abadiy zarar yetkazishi mumkin. Aytishlaricha, "Ishonchni qurish uchun yillar kerak, buzish uchun soniyalar va tiklash uchun abadiyat". Ishonchli inson bo'lish - bu inson ega bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan eng qimmatli fazilatlardan biridir.

questions.prompt: Smartphones Should Be Banned in Classrooms
questions.sampleA1:
Phone no good in class.

I have phone.

Teacher say no.
questions.sampleA2:
I think phones in class are bad.

Because students play games.

And they don't listen to the teacher.

But sometimes phones are useful.

Like for talking to parents.
questions.sampleB1:
I think smartphones in classrooms is a difficult question.

On the one hand, phones can be distracting. Students might use them to text or go on social media instead of learning.

However, phones can also be useful for school.

For example, you can use them to look up information or use educational apps.

So, maybe there should be rules about when you can use your phone.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so the statement here is that smartphones should be banned in classrooms, and I can honestly see both sides of the argument. On the one hand, there's no denying that phones can be a huge distraction. Let's face it, if a student has a phone on their desk, they're far more likely to be scrolling through social media or texting than paying attention to the lesson. It's not fair on the students who genuinely want to learn. On top of that, phones can be used for cheating in exams, and constant notifications can really disrupt the whole class. So, from that point of view, a ban makes a lot of sense. On the other hand, I think an outright ban might be throwing the baby out with the bathwater. The thing is, smartphones are incredibly powerful learning tools. Students can look up information in seconds, use educational apps, and collaborate on projects. For a lot of teachers, that opens up all sorts of creative possibilities. What's more, in an emergency, being able to reach a parent is genuinely reassuring. All things considered, I'd say a complete ban is a bit heavy-handed. Personally, I reckon the sensible approach is to meet in the middle. Schools could allow phones for specific, teacher-led activities, but keep them switched off and put away the rest of the time. You know, banning things outright rarely works with teenagers anyway. At the end of the day, it's all about teaching young people to use technology responsibly, rather than banning it altogether.

Bir tomondan, telefonlar chalg'ituvchi bo'lishi mumkin. O'quvchilar ulardan o'qish o'rniga xabar yozish yoki ijtimoiy tarmoqlarga kirish uchun foydalanishi mumkin.

Biroq, telefonlar maktab uchun ham foydali bo'lishi mumkin.

Misol uchun, ulardan ma'lumot qidirish yoki ta'limiy ilovalardan foydalanish uchun foydalanishingiz mumkin.

Shunday ekan, telefoningizdan qachon foydalanish mumkinligi haqida qoidalar bo'lishi kerakdir.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Sinf xonalarida smartfonlarni taqiqlash mavzusi juda murakkab.

To‘g‘ri, telefonlar o‘quvchilarni o‘qishga diqqatini jamlashiga xalaqit beradigan asosiy chalg‘ituvchi omil bo‘lishi mumkin. Ular boshqalar uchun ham ta’lim muhitini buzishi mumkin.

Biroq, smartfonlar ta’limiy afzalliklarni ham taklif etadi. O‘quvchilar tezda ma’lumot olishlari, o‘quv dasturlaridan foydalanishlari va loyihalar ustida hamkorlik qilishlari mumkin.

Bundan tashqari, ba’zi hollarda ular ota-onalar bilan aloqa qilish uchun zarur.

Ehtimol, murosaga kelish kerakdir, masalan, telefonlardan muayyan ta’limiy faoliyatlar uchun foydalanishga ruxsat berish, lekin darslar davomida ulardan foydalanishni cheklash.

Potensial foyda va kamchiliklarni ham hisobga olish muhim.

questions.sampleAnswer:
The question of whether smartphones should be banned in classrooms is highly debated, and I'd like to explore both sides of this argument.
Those in favor of banning smartphones make several valid points. Firstly, phones are a major source of distraction. Students may be tempted to check social media, play games, or text friends instead of paying attention to lessons. This significantly reduces their focus and academic performance. Secondly, a phone-free environment encourages more face-to-face interaction between students and teachers, fostering better communication skills. Additionally, banning phones prevents cheating during exams and tests, ensuring academic integrity.
On the other hand, there are compelling arguments against a complete ban. Smartphones can serve as powerful educational tools – students can access online resources, educational apps, and research materials instantly. They're also essential for emergencies; parents need to reach their children, and vice versa. Furthermore, completely restricting phones may seem overly controlling and doesn't teach students self-discipline and responsible use of technology.
In my opinion, a balanced approach would be ideal – allowing phones during breaks but requiring them to be silent and stored away during lessons. This teaches students to manage their device usage responsibly.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Smartfonlar sinf xonalarida taqiqlanishi kerakmi degan savol juda ko'p bahs-munozaralarga sabab bo'lmoqda va men bu bahsning har ikki tomonini o'rganmoqchiman.

Smartfonlarni taqiqlash tarafdorlari bir nechta asosli dalillarni keltirishadi. Birinchidan, telefonlar diqqatni chalg'ituvchi asosiy manba hisoblanadi. Talabalar darslarga e'tibor berish o'rniga ijtimoiy tarmoqlarni tekshirish, o'yinlar o'ynash yoki do'stlariga xabar yozishga vasvasaga tushishlari mumkin. Bu ularning diqqatini va o'zlashtirish darajasini sezilarli darajada pasaytiradi. Ikkinchidan, telefonsiz muhit talabalar va o'qituvchilar o'rtasida yuzma-yuz muloqotni rag'batlantiradi va bu esa yaxshiroq muloqot ko'nikmalarini shakllantiradi. Bundan tashqari, telefonlarni taqiqlash imtihonlar va testlar paytida aldashning oldini oladi va o'quv jarayonining halolligini ta'minlaydi.

Boshqa tomondan, to'liq taqiqqa qarshi ham ishonarli dalillar mavjud. Smartfonlar kuchli o'quv vositasi bo'lib xizmat qilishi mumkin – talabalar onlayn resurslarga, ta'limiy ilovalarga va tadqiqot materiallariga bir zumda kirishlari mumkin. Ular, shuningdek, favqulodda vaziyatlar uchun ham zarur; ota-onalar farzandlari bilan bog'lanishlari kerak va aksincha. Bundan tashqari, telefonlarni butunlay cheklash haddan tashqari nazoratdek tuyulishi mumkin va talabalarga o'z-o'zini intizomga solishni va texnologiyadan mas'uliyatli foydalanishni o'rgatmaydi.

Menimcha, muvozanatli yondashuv ideal bo'lar edi – tanaffus paytida telefonlarga ruxsat berish, lekin darslar paytida ularni o'chirilgan va yig'ishtirilgan holda saqlashni talab qilish. Bu talabalarga o'z qurilmalaridan foydalanishni mas'uliyat bilan boshqarishni o'rgatadi.
